1.verse_text: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
1.why: Gen 12:2 addresses Abraham himself ('I will make you into a great nation'), not Abraham's seed, which is the card's subject.

2.why: Josh 7:20 has Achan confess 'I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel', while the card records only his tribe, his father and his stoning.

3.flagged_fact: filled with the Spirit of God
3.verse_text: And He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,
3.why: The 'him' filled with the Spirit of God in Exod 35:31 is Bezalel (Exod 35:30), not Oholiab, who is named later in 35:34.

5.verse_text: Then Asa cried out to the LORD his God: “O LORD, there is no one besides You to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God. Do not let a mere mortal prevail against You.”
5.why: Asa himself says 'we rely on You' and 'we have come against this multitude', and no card line records his reliance on the LORD; the Cushite identification of the multitude comes from 14:9, not the quoted verse.

6.why: Psalm 73:1's superscription attributes one psalm to Asaph; the verse nowhere says he wrote many of the Psalms.

22.why: 2 Kings 5:1 opens by identifying Naaman as commander of the army of the king of Aram; the card's three lines (Gehazi, Elisha, Jordan) never say it.

23.flagged_fact: He was the cupbearer to the king
23.verse_text: O Lord, may Your ear be attentive to my prayer and to the prayers of Your servants who delight to revere Your name. Give Your servant success this day, I pray, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man.” (At that time I was the cupbearer to the king.)
23.why: Neh 1:11 states 'I was the cupbearer to the king'; none of the card's lines (wall, father Azbuk, Beth-zur) mention that role, which is his defining position.
